title: Search a sorted 2-D matrix
statement: Each row is sorted and each row's first value is greater than the previous row's last. Return whether target is present, in O(log(rows · cols)).
hints: Read row by row, it's one sorted array of length rows × cols.
Index k maps to (k // cols, k % cols).

solution.explanation: Treat the matrix as a virtual sorted array of length rc and binary-search it, mapping index k to row k // c, column k % c. Recognising a disguised sorted array is the point.
solution.python:
def search_matrix(m, target):
    if not m or not m[0]: return False
    R_, C = len(m), len(m[0]); lo, hi = 0, R_ * C
    while lo < hi:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if m[mid // C][mid % C] < target: lo = mid + 1
        else: hi = mid
    return lo < R_ * C and m[lo // C][lo % C] == target
